title: API 653 Training in Pasadena, TX: Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 653 exam prep for Pasadena tank inspectors: truck-rack, ship channel and chemical terminals, worked shell examples and instructor Q&A.
h1: API 653 Training in Pasadena, Texas: Online Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector Exam Prep for Racks, Terminals and Plant Tank Farms
html:
API 653 exam prep for Pasadena tank inspectors

Pasadena's tanks come in every shape the API 653 inspector deals with: big floating-roof product tanks on the ship channel, fixed-roof distillate and blendstock tanks behind truck racks, small stainless chemical tanks in Bayport, and feed and intermediate tanks inside the refinery and the chemical plants. Each atmospheric steel tank built to API 650 or its predecessor needs routine in-service checks, periodic external and internal inspections and an inspector's call on repairs, alterations and reconstruction. This page is for terminal technicians, refinery and chemical-plant inspectors, tank contractors and NDT crews in Pasadena, La Porte and Seabrook preparing for the API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector examination.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Pasadena. The API 653 course is self-paced online, with an instructor answering your questions, so you can study between floor scans, roof inspections and out-of-service jobs. API sets eligibility under Annex D of API 653, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and the course grants no certification.

Pasadena tank sites, by the operators' own figures

Published terminal sheets give a clear picture of the storage inside the city and on its edges.

Storage sites in and around Pasadena (from operator publications)
SiteWhat the operator publishesWhat it means for a 653 inspector
Kinder Morgan Jefferson Street truck rack, Pasadena19 tanks of 10,000 to 100,000 barrels, about 970,000 barrels in all; gasoline blendstocks, ULSD, biodiesel (B5 and B99), ethanol (E-10 and E-100) and jet fuel; nine automated truck loading baysMid-sized product tanks turning over quickly, ethanol and biodiesel service, rack piping and secondary containment
Kinder Morgan Pasadena terminal, ship channelA 341-acre site whose tanks range up to 300,000 barrels, linked to the Colonial and Explorer pipelines and served by ship and barge docksLarge-diameter tanks, floating roofs and seals, settlement surveys and long bottom inspections
Odfjell Terminals Houston, near the entrance of the Houston Ship Channel126 tanks for chemicals, petroleum, acids and edible oils (73 mild steel, 11 coated, 42 stainless steel), plus 2 stainless spheres; heated, cooled and insulated service availableSmall and mid-sized chemical tanks, stainless construction, coatings and insulation; spheres fall outside API 653
Refinery and chemical plantsChevron's Pasadena refinery, Chevron Phillips Chemical's Pasadena Plastics Complex and the Bayport district's plantsCrude, intermediate, feed and product tanks inside operating units, often inspected during outages

The spheres are worth a moment because they turn up as exam distractors. API 653's scope is written around carbon and low-alloy steel tanks built to API 650 or its predecessor API 12C; pressurised spheres are pressure vessels and belong elsewhere. The stainless tanks raise a subtler scope question, so note exactly which materials the scope sentence names and how an owner may apply the standard's principles beyond them. Read the scope section until you can say confidently what is in and what is out.

What Pasadena service asks of a tank inspector

Ethanol and biodiesel tanks

A rack that stores E-100 brings ethanol stress corrosion cracking into the picture, and API RP 571 describes when fuel-grade ethanol cracks carbon steel and which locations are most at risk. Biodiesel and blended fuels bring their own questions about water, sludge and microbiologically influenced corrosion on tank bottoms. Learn these from RP 571 and RP 575, and know which inspection methods find each kind of damage.

Stainless and coated chemical tanks

Chemical terminals store products that would ruin bare carbon steel, so stainless steel construction, internal linings and coatings are common. API RP 652 covers linings of tank bottoms, and API RP 651 covers cathodic protection of tank bottoms. The exam tests when a lining or a cathodic protection system can justify a longer bottom inspection interval, and what records the inspector needs to rely on it.

Soft ground, rain and the bottom

The Gulf Coast's clay soils, heavy rain and high water table make foundations, drainage and bottom-side corrosion central to local tank work. Settlement evaluation, edge settlement and the critical zone near the shell all appear on the exam; practise reading settlement survey data and applying the evaluation rules in API 653's annex on settlement.

Repairs, alterations and the hydrotest decision

Busy product tanks are modified often: new nozzles for blending lines, replaced shell plates, new bottoms laid over old ones, roof conversions. API 653 separates repairs from alterations and both from reconstruction, and each category carries its own rules on weld examination, documentation and whether a full hydrostatic test is needed afterwards. The exam regularly presents a job description and asks whether a hydrotest can be waived, and on what conditions, such as the engineer's evaluation, the extent of examination of new welds and the brittle fracture assessment. Learn the brittle fracture decision sequence in its own section of API 653 as well, because it is how the code decides whether an older tank can safely return to service after a change in operation or a repair.

Air rules on floating roofs

Harris County lies in the Houston-Galveston-Brazoria area, where the TCEQ's storage tank rules in 30 TAC Chapter 115, Subchapter B, Division 1 control VOC emissions according to tank size and vapour pressure. Those rules set requirements for fittings and seals, limit floating-roof landings and include testing, inspection and monitoring requirements. They are not on the API 653 exam, but every terminal inspector in Pasadena works with them, and they explain why roof seals and fittings get so much attention locally.

A worked example for the open-book half

Take a hypothetical product tank, 100 ft in diameter, with a maximum liquid level of 48 ft, six 8 ft courses, specific gravity 0.85, unknown plate material and a joint efficiency of 1.0. These are practice figures only.

Minimum thickness of the bottom two courses

For unknown material, API 653 takes the allowable stress for the first and second courses as 23,600 psi. The whole-course formula is tmin = 2.6 (H − 1) D G ÷ (S E), with H measured from the bottom of the course being evaluated. First course: 2.6 × 47 × 100 × 0.85 ÷ 23,600 = 0.440 in. Second course, H = 40 ft: 2.6 × 39 × 100 × 0.85 ÷ 23,600 = 0.365 in. From the third course upward the higher stress of 26,000 psi applies: 2.6 × 31 × 100 × 0.85 ÷ 26,000 = 0.263 in.

Corrosion rate and remaining life

The lowest first-course reading has gone from 0.512 in. to 0.480 in. over eight years, a rate of 0.004 in. per year. Remaining life is (0.480 − 0.440) ÷ 0.004 = 10 years. Keep a close eye on the units in such questions; mixing millimetres and inches is a deliberate trap.

How high can the tank be filled?

Suppose the second course has thinned so that, after deducting the corrosion expected before the next inspection, 0.340 in. remains. Rearranging gives H = S E t ÷ (2.6 D G) + 1 = 23,600 × 0.340 ÷ (2.6 × 100 × 0.85) + 1 = 8,024 ÷ 221 + 1 = 37.3 ft. That height is measured from the bottom of the second course, which sits 8 ft above the floor, so the safe fill height for the tank is about 45.3 ft, below the 48 ft design level. Candidates who forget to add the course elevation give 37.3 ft and lose the mark.

The national API 653 training page works through locally thinned areas, pitting rules and bottom projections in more depth, and the API 653 shell minimum thickness guide explains the formulas line by line.

Routes into API 653 from Pasadena jobs

Annex D of API 653 combines education and experience: one year of supervising or performing tank inspection with an engineering or technology bachelor's degree; two years in design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of tanks, one of them in inspection, with a two-year degree or certificate; three years with a high school diploma; and five or more years without formal education. Experience must be recent and gained while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. The API 653 certification requirements page covers the detail.

Local candidates often come from MFL floor-scanning crews, UT shell-survey technicians, tank construction and repair contractors, terminal operations staff who move into integrity roles, and refinery or chemical plant inspectors adding tanks to their scope. San Jacinto College's Central Campus in Pasadena offers inspection and NDT programmes that give a structured start before those working years. For technicians, Atlantis's NDT training for Pasadena covers ASNT SNT-TC-1A methods, which is separate from the API course.

Studying API 653 around terminal schedules

Out-of-service tank inspections, roof repairs and rack projects come in bursts, so plan study in phases rather than weeks:

  • Codes first. Read API 653 and the parts of API 650 the Body of Knowledge lists until you can find any clause quickly, paying attention to repairs, alterations, reconstruction, hydrostatic testing and the inspection intervals.
  • Recommended practices. Cover RP 575, RP 571's listed mechanisms, RP 577, RP 651 and RP 652, then the ASME Section V and IX material for your window.
  • Calculations. Shell tmin, fill height, corroded areas, pits, settlement and bottom projections, repeated until each takes a few minutes.
  • Practice papers. Timed, closed-book then open-book with the PDFs, with every doubtful answer sent to the instructor.

Use the API exam schedule to pick a window, and the API 653 tank inspection guide for the background on how in-service tank inspection works.

Other ways to prepare, and where the course fits

Pasadena candidates can choose between in-person exam-prep classes run by commercial trainers across the Houston area, a college route that builds inspection skills over several semesters, and coaching from an employer's own tank specialists where that exists. Each has its place. The self-paced online course with instructor Q&A suits people whose tank jobs come at unpredictable times, who want to rehearse the open-book searches many times, or who are studying well ahead of their window.

Exam day and employer sponsorship

When API approves your application, you schedule a Prometric appointment; Prometric lists test centres in and around Pasadena and greater Houston. The day lasts 7.5 hours, with 170 questions split into closed-book and open-book parts and the code PDFs provided on screen for the second. API reports results and the certification runs for three years. Terminal operators and contractors can enrol several inspectors together; fees are quoted on request through the enquiry link on this page. Owners who need inspection can also ask Atlantis about UT, MT, PT and VT work in the US, and about remote RBI for storage tanks.

faq.q: Can I attend API 653 classes in Pasadena?
faq.a: Not with Atlantis. Atlantis has no classroom there: there is no Atlantis classroom in Pasadena for any API course, and API 653 prep runs self-paced online with an instructor answering questions. You study API 653, API 650 and the recommended practices on your own schedule, which works around tank outages and rack projects. The exam itself is in person at a Prometric test centre after API approves your application.

faq.q: Are the spheres at Pasadena chemical terminals covered by API 653?
faq.a: No. API 653 is written for aboveground storage tanks built to API 650 or its predecessor API 12C. Pressurised spheres and bullets are pressure vessels and fall outside its scope. Scope questions are popular on the exam, so read the opening section of API 653 closely and be ready to exclude equipment that looks like a tank but is not one under the code.

faq.q: Will I be examined on ethanol cracking if I work at a Pasadena rack?
faq.a: It is described in API RP 571, and whether it is examined depends on the mechanisms listed for your exam window. Check the Body of Knowledge for your window. In Pasadena it is a practical topic as well, because racks such as Kinder Morgan's Jefferson Street terminal publish E-100 ethanol among their products.

faq.q: Does my MFL floor-scanning experience count towards API 653?
faq.a: It can count as performing tank inspection activities if API accepts the role you document, and if you were employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. Record the tanks, dates, methods and your responsibilities, and have a supervisor confirm them. The certification requirements page explains the education and experience combinations.

faq.q: Do TCEQ rules appear on the API 653 exam?
faq.a: No. The exam tests API 653 and the documents in the Body of Knowledge. The TCEQ's Chapter 115 storage tank rules still matter in Pasadena because Harris County is in the Houston-Galveston-Brazoria area, and they cover seals, fittings, floating-roof landings and monitoring. Treat them as job knowledge, separate from exam preparation.

faq.q: Which API 653 calculations trip candidates up most?
faq.a: Fill height, because candidates forget to add the elevation of the course being evaluated; locally thinned areas, where the corrosion allowance until the next inspection is left out; and bottom projections, where the wrong reading or rate is used. The course works each one with practice numbers and explains the wrong answers that appear among the options.

faq.q: Can a Pasadena terminal operator sponsor several inspectors?
faq.a: Yes. An employer can enrol a group, and each person studies at their own pace with access to the instructor. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually with their own experience record, and API decides on eligibility.

faq.q: Where do Pasadena candidates take the API 653 exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre chosen when you schedule within your approved window. Prometric lists test centres in and around Pasadena and greater Houston; confirm the current list on its site when you book. Windows and application deadlines are kept on the exam schedule page.
